title: Drone accident and safety event reports from public safety BVLOS waiver holders (2024–present)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Drone accident and safety event reports from public safety BVLOS waiver holders (2024–present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

For January 1, 2024, through the date of processing:

1. All reports submitted to the FAA through FAADroneZone under Special Provision 29 of any Part 107 Certificate of Waiver and Authorization waiving 14 CFR §§ 107.31, 107.39, and 107.145 in combination (the public safety organization template issued by the Emerging Technologies Division, AFS-700, and exemplified by waiver numbers 107W-2026-01670 and 107W-2026-02013), including: (a) events reported as meeting the criteria of § 107.9 "Safety Event" reporting; (b) events in which an unmanned aircraft was operated within 500 feet vertically or horizontally of an aircraft with a person on board, including reported closest-point-of-approach distances; and (c) reported loss-of-control events.

2. All accident reports submitted under 14 CFR § 107.9 by any holder of a Part 107 Certificate of Waiver that either (a) waives exactly 14 CFR §§ 107.31, 107.39, and 107.145 (including holders of the earlier template exemplified by waiver number 107W-2025-01731), or (b) recorded "Public Safety Organization" as the Type of Operator on the waiver application. A holder meeting either condition is within the request.

3. Any flight-time record obtained by the FAA from a holder under Special Provision 25 of the template described in item 1, and any record in the Accident/Incident Data System (AIDS) or any parallel or successor sUAS dataset corresponding to the events in items 1 and 2.

4. All accident, incident, or mishap reports submitted to the FAA under any special provision or condition of a Part 91 Public Aircraft/Public Safety Operations Certificate of Waiver (waiver of 14 CFR 91.113(b) and/or 91.119), or of any Tactical BVLOS or First Responder BVLOS certificate of waiver or authorization in effect during the period.

If the FAA cannot filter items 1 through 3 by waiver instrument or Type of Operator without manual review, I will accept a complete export of all sUAS accident, safety event, and AIDS records for the period, provided the export includes every field identifying the associated waiver or certificate number, waiver template, Type of Operator, and operator name, so that operations under the named instruments can be distinguished.

Please produce records as a native database export (CSV, XLSX, or JSON) with all fields, rather than PDF images, per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3)(B). I do not object to redaction of individual home addresses, personal phone numbers, or personal email addresses. Operator or agency name, waiver or certificate number, date, location, aircraft make and model, injury and damage descriptions, closest-point-of-approach distances, and narrative should be released as reasonably segregable.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

HCvP

title: OAG Executive Cover-Up: Chief Deputy AG Seth Rosenthal's Digital Telemetry & Case #00085753

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: erika.stillabower@dc.gov (via MuckRock)
CC: bpinto@dccouncil.gov; twhite@dccouncil.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.gov; chenderson@dccouncil.gov; lkasomo@dccouncil.gov
Subject: D.C. FOIA Request: Executive Suite Communications, Telemetry Logs, and Case #00085753 (Fred Gamble Jr. / City Lending Inc.)

Ms. Stillabower,

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-532), I am formally requesting public records related to OAG Consumer and Tenant Response Case #00085753, as well as the internal communications of the Immediate Office of the Attorney General.

On July 5, 2026, I submitted a comprehensive dossier documenting predatory lending and ongoing foreclosure fraud by City Lending Inc. (NMLS: 1045126). Just three days later, on July 8, 2026, the OAG formally closed this case with an automated notification falsely claiming the matter was a "business-to-business" or "condo/co-op/HOA" governance issue. 

Because I am an individual homeowner and this is a residential mortgage, this closure was factually baseless. Furthermore, independently captured digital telemetry (Mailsuite tracking data) confirms that Chief Deputy Attorney General Seth Rosenthal extensively opened, monitored, and read my case communications during this exact period while allowing the case to be summarily closed via a false administrative pretext.

To expose this executive-level suppression, I am requesting the following specific records:

1. Executive Telemetry and Routing Logs: All internal forwarding records, server routing logs, read receipts, and Microsoft Teams communications generated by or sent to the Immediate Office (specifically Chief Deputy Attorney General Seth Rosenthal and Attorney General Brian Schwalb) detailing their active monitoring of my submissions regarding Case #00085753.

2. Case Closure Authorization: The complete, unredacted intake file, investigator notes, and formal closure authorization for Case #00085753, including any supervisory directives instructing the Consumer Protection Unit to utilize a "business-to-business" or "HOA governance" rejection template for a residential mortgage fraud complaint.

3. Keyword Search (Emails and Communications): All internal emails, attachments, and chat transcripts sent or received by Attorney General Brian Schwalb, Chief Deputy Attorney General Seth Rosenthal, or Investigator Timothy Shirey between July 1, 2026, and August 15, 2026, containing any of the following terms:
- "00085753"
- "Fred Gamble"
- "1490 Morris"
- "City Lending"
- "Seth Rosenthal"
- "Jorge Campodonico"

Fee Waiver Request:
Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full waiver of search and reproduction fees. Disclosure of these records directly serves the public interest of the District of Columbia by illuminating the direct involvement of the OAG’s executive leadership in suppressing investigations into unlicensed shadow-lending operations targeting Ward 8. This request is non-commercial.

Format & Statutory Deadline:
Please provide all responsive materials electronically in their native digital format, preserving all metadata. As required by D.C. FOIA, a determination is required within 15 business days. Because Case #00085753 was officially closed on July 8, 2026, statutory exemptions under D.C. Code § 2-534 regarding ongoing law enforcement proceedings do not apply. Any invocation of the "deliberative process" privilege must be explicitly justified per document.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

Ms. Stillabower,

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-532), I am formally requesting public records related to OAG Consumer Protection Case #00051903, which was active between 2022 and April 2023 and primarily handled by Investigator Timothy Shirey.

During this investigation, the OAG facilitated a $5,800 settlement regarding a contractor dispute for stair repairs at my residence. However, the OAG simultaneously severed, suppressed, or ignored the concurrent predatory lending and mortgage fraud allegations I submitted under the exact same file against City Lending Inc. (NMLS: 1045126) and Jorge Campodonico.

I am requesting the following specific records to illuminate this administrative severance:

1. The Complete Investigative File: The full, unredacted intake notes, investigator logs, constituent service records, and closure authorization forms for Case #00051903.

2. The Severance Directives: Any internal memoranda, supervisory directives, or communications explaining why the structural damage complaint was addressed and settled, while the predatory lending and mortgage fraud components of the exact same file were ignored or dismissed.

3. Keyword Search (Emails and Communications): All internal emails, attachments, and Microsoft Teams or chat transcripts sent or received by Investigator Timothy Shirey or his direct supervisors between January 1, 2022, and April 30, 2023, containing any of the following terms in relation to Case #00051903:
- "Fred Gamble"
- "1490 Morris"
- "City Lending"
- "Jorge Campodonico"
- "Stairs" or "$5,800"

Fee Waiver Request:
